purpose: Design inputs for TwoSpace, not evidence of outcomes for this app.
scope: Remote relationships are complete relationships. Meeting in person and closing distance are optional, never assumed goals.

sources.title: Intimacy in Long-Distance Relationships over Video Chat
sources.method: Semi-structured interviews with 14 people, ages 19–35; only two participants were partners of each other.
sources.finding: Participants shared ordinary activities and background companionship as well as conversation through video.
sources.limits: Existing video-chat users, mostly North American and technically comfortable; qualitative accounts, not an intervention trial.
sources.designInference: Support shared activities without requiring continuous conversation. Existing calling tools can complement the app.

sources.title: Understanding Family Communication across Time Zones
sources.authors: Xiang Cao, Abigail Sellen, A. J. Bernheim Brush, David Kirk, Darren Edge and Xianghua Ding
sources.method: Interviews with 14 people from 12 households communicating across differences of 3–12 hours.
sources.finding: People used overlapping free time and informal routines; travel and changes to schedules disrupted coordination.
sources.limits: Exploratory self-report study covering family relationships beyond couples; communication tools have changed.
sources.designInference: Display both local dates and times. Allow schedule exceptions and activities that can continue later.

sources.title: Bedtime Window: A Field Study Connecting Bedrooms of Long-Distance Couples Using a Slow Photo-Stream and Shared Real-Time Inking
sources.authors: Jan Kučera, James Scott, Siân Lindley and Patrick Olivier
sources.method: Small field study of a situated photo-stream and drawing device; published abstract inspected.
sources.finding: The abstract reports perceived remote presence, privacy balance and collaborative use of shared inking.
sources.limits: Specialized hardware and a small sample. Findings do not establish outcomes for a browser-based drawing tool.
sources.designInference: Offer deliberate photo sharing and a shared drawing surface; do not activate cameras automatically.

sources.title: Partnership through Play: Investigating How Long-Distance Couples Use Digital Games to Facilitate Intimacy
sources.authors: Nisha Devasia, Adrian Rodriguez, Logan Tuttle and Julie A. Kientz
sources.method: Diaries, interviews and a design activity with 13 couples who already played together at least weekly.
sources.finding: Couples differed in cooperative and competitive preferences and used game mechanics for affection and shared meaning.
sources.limits: Small self-selected gaming sample, mostly in their twenties and primarily American context; not representative of all couples.
sources.designInference: Include creative activities alongside competitive games. Let people save selected moments and take turns at their own pace.

sources.title: Absence Makes the Communication Grow Fonder
sources.authors: L. Crystal Jiang and Jeffrey T. Hancock
sources.method: One-week diary study of 63 heterosexual dating couples, including 30 long-distance couples.
sources.finding: Participants used multiple communication channels; disclosure and perceptions varied by medium and relationship context.
sources.limits: Mostly college students, short observation and self-report. The authors explicitly state the design cannot establish causal relationships over time.
sources.designInference: Make short mobile contributions convenient and offer optional prompts without prescribing communication frequency.

sources.title: Privacy or Transparency? Negotiated Smartphone Access as a Signifier of Trust in Romantic Relationships
sources.authors: Periwinkle Doerfler, Kieron Ivy Turk, Chris Geeng, Damon McCoy, Jeffrey Ackerman and Molly Dragiewicz
sources.method: Authors' survey of 531 respondents, supplemented by analysis of a 2,050-person Norton survey.
sources.finding: Preferences for partner device access varied; respondents emphasized consensual, negotiated boundaries.
sources.limits: The recruited sample was not representative. Long-distance and online-only respondents were excluded from partner-device-access questions; this is adjacent privacy evidence.
sources.designInference: Use separate accounts, explicit publication, private drafts and clear leave/delete controls. Avoid compulsory read receipts, location sharing and activity scores.

productBoundaries: No claim that this app improves relationship health, reduces loneliness or prevents separation.
No relationship score, response deadline, compulsory streak or assumed reunion countdown.
Research-informed features remain design hypotheses to evaluate through usability testing.
